extracted.intended_audience: readers, librarians, bibliographers and researchers of early-20th-century short fiction; editors compiling bibliographies
extracted.subtask_description: A bibliographic index of short stories listing authors, story titles, periodical citations, dates, and editorial annotations/symbols for a given year. Used to locate, cross-reference, and mark notable items within the yearbook's corpus of short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol/annotation markers next to entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are annotated with symbols immediately before titles or author lines such as '*', '**', '***', '♦', '♦♦', '♦♦♦'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols appear frequently (e.g., '***Lonely Places. Pict. R. Dec.', '♦Trouble with Martha, The. Harp. M. Dec.'). This page does not include a legend explaining the meaning; they are editorial annotations likely indicating emphasis, quality, prominence, reprint/translation status, or recommendation. No on-page scoring guidance is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author entry format (name and life‑dates / cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author lines often show the author name followed by birth-year (and sometimes a hyphen) in parentheses, and may include cross-reference notes such as '(See 1915 and 1916.)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Butler, Ellis Parker. (1869-        .) (See 1915 and 1916.)' and 'Cather, Willa Sibert. (1875-        .) (See 1915 and 1916.)'. This indicates the index records author identity and points readers to other yearly indexes or entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title + periodical citation + date format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each story entry lists the title followed by an abbreviated periodical title and then a month or full date (e.g., 'Pict. R. Dec.', 'Col. Nov. 17').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example entries: '***Long Vacation, The. Pict. R. Sept.' and 'Chasm, The. S. E. P. Dec. 8.' Periodical abbreviations (Col., Harp. M., S. E. P., Atl., etc.) are used consistently; the pattern is Title. Periodical_Abbrev. Month [Day]. This is the principal bibliographic convention on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical organization by initial letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are grouped under single-letter headings (e.g., 'C', 'D', 'H') representing the alphabetical division of the index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instance, the chunk shows the heading 'C' then many author entries beginning with C; later 'D', etc. This is the organizational principle for locating authors/titles alphabetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical editorial qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses are used to provide supplementary information: alternate/real names, pseudonyms, editorial qualifiers like '(R.)', and explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '" Byrne, Donn." (Bryan Oswald Donn-Byrne.)', and story entries with '(R.)' after the title (e.g., 'East and West. (R.) Mir. Jan. 19.'). The page uses parentheses for author biographical data and for brief editorial qualifiers; the exact meaning of qualifiers like '(R.)' is not defined on this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to other volumes/years/pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Some author lines include explicit cross-references such as '(See 1915 and 1916.)' indicating where related entries or additional information may be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This instructs users to consult other yearbook volumes or sections for more entries on the same author. Example: 'Camp (Charles) Wadsworth. (See 1915 and 1916.)' — the entry itself may be brief and relies on cross-referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of periodical abbreviation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations for periodicals are used throughout (e.g., 'Har p. M.', 'Col.', 'Pict. R.', 'S. E. P.', 'E. W.'), forming a compact citation style for the index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers must interpret these abbreviations (not expanded on this page chunk). Examples: '***Man Who Went Back, The. L. H. J. June.' and '***Foundling, The. Col. Oct. 27.' The index assumes familiarity with the yearbook's periodical abbreviation key elsewhere.
